entry.title: No Bones Broken, No Crime Committed: Inside the Taliban’s New Rules on Violence Against Women
entry.summary:
KABUL, April 21 (IPS) - The Taliban have announced new laws that effectively legalise domestic violence against women and children. Afghanistan’s supreme leader, Mullah Hibatullah Akhundzada, signed a decree introducing a new criminal code in January. It contains three parts, ten chapters, and 119 articles that legalise violence, codify social inequality, and introduce punitive measures widely condemned as a return to slavery.

Read the full story, “No Bones Broken, No Crime Committed: Inside the Taliban’s New Rules on Violence Against Women”, on globalissues.org →

entry.title: Trump’s Apocalyptic Rhetoric Echoes Nuclear Annihilation
entry.summary:
NEW YORK, April 21 (IPS) - It is hard to exaggerate the dire implications of Trump’s April 7 post on Truth Social, stating that a civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again,” if no deal is reached with Iran. Such a damning statement implies that he would use ‘weapons of mass destruction,’ i.e., nuclear, to execute his threat.

entry.summary:
